primitives.name: Pressure Split Cluster
primitives.verbatim_quote: **The pressure-split cluster (dossiers #1, #8, #12, #13)** — four independent accounts converged tonight on the same measurement family: QB EPA split by pressured vs kept-clean (and vs blitz).
primitives.assumptions: Assumes clean/cleaned data from nflverse pressure flags and EPA metrics.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breakdown occurs when pressure definitions conflict across vendors or when QB performance is driven by quick-game schematics rather than pure pocket presence.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE's situational reasoning by decomposing quarterback performance into components attributable to protection quality versus inherent skill. Maps to GSI's conformal inference by treating pressure states as conditioning variables to estimate expected EPA distributions.
layer2.telemetry: GSE should hold NFLVERSE pressure flags. Verification metric: compare QB rankings within clean vs pressured buckets across multiple weeks.

primitives.name: SCRACK
primitives.verbatim_quote: **SCRACK (dossiers #6, #7, #9)** — a named, defined composite (SCRAMBLE EPA + SACK EPA, championed by @schwartzsteins) with a full-league bar chart and a worked outlier case (Bo Nix).
primitives.assumptions: Assumes accurate SCRAMBLE EPA and SACK EPA measurements without noise.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breakdown occurs when scrambling plays are infrequent or when sack penalties significantly distort the SACK EPA component.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE's situational reasoning by quantifying a quarterback's ability to avoid negative outcomes (via scrambles) and penalty-free efficiency (against sacks). Maps to GSI's conformal inference by pricing the combined impact of these two distinct failure modes into a single metric.
layer2.telemetry: GSE should have play-level scramble and sack data. Verification metric: compute SCRACK for all QBs and validate the Bo Nix outlier case.

primitives.name: Predicted Coverage Shells
primitives.verbatim_quote: **@KoalatyStats' Predicted Coverage Shells + Predicted Pressure models (dossier #11)** — the Week 8 Substack (verified live, published Oct 30 20:41 UTC) shows a working pre-game *predicted* coverage-shell and *predicted* pressure product with per-player matchup derivatives (coverage-shell-adjusted TPRR).
primitives.assumptions: Assumes accurate prediction models for coverage shells and pressure based on historical defensive tendencies.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breakdown occurs when defenses employ unpredictable personnel groupings or when injuries cause last-minute lineup changes that invalidate the predicted matchups.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE's situational reasoning by providing predictive inputs for defensive coverage assignments and pressure schemes, enabling state-transition calculations for offensive success probabilities. Maps to GSI's conformal inference by incorporating uncertainty in defensive predictions into probabilistic forecasts of offensive outcomes.
layer2.telemetry: GSE needs access to KoalatyStats' Substack or similar predictive models. Verification metric: compare predicted coverage shells against actual defensive formations in subsequent games.

primitives.verbatim_quote: **@The_Coach_A — nub-Trips "shove" call (dossier #10)** — a named split-field c
primitives.assumptions: Assumes the effectiveness of the shove concept depends on proper execution and receiver recognition of the defender's alignment.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Breakdown occurs when defenders recognize the formation early and adjust their coverage, negating the intended misdirection.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE's situational reasoning by formalizing the strategic interaction between offensive line assignments and defensive coverage shells, creating a decision tree for optimal play selection. Maps to GSI's conformal inference by treating the success of the shove call as a binary outcome conditioned on specific defensive alignments, allowing for probability estimation.
layer2.telemetry: GSE should track the frequency and success rates of the nub-trips shove call. Verification metric: analyze game film to confirm the correlation between the call and favorable outcomes.
